text:
release-lead: Quick note for this week's train 12: we've updated the rollout ownership matrix and added an explicit "bridge" role for cross-team coordination during multi-service rollouts. Details below, please ack.

nina: What does the bridge role do exactly?

release-lead: Bridge = single point for cross-cutting comms during a rollout window. Responsibilities: monitor end-to-end SLO signals, consolidate triage, coordinate cross-team rollbacks, and publish timeline updates to #eng-releases. Bridge is not primary oncall; it's an orchestration role.

theo: How do we assign bridge for a given release?

release-lead: Policy: owning team nominates bridge in the deploy ticket. If no nomination, release-lead assigns from the oncall rotation. We'll start with a 1-week trial.

oncall: Will bridge be paged? I don't want extra pages.

release-lead: Bridge receives high-level alerts (summary only) and chat notifications; paged only if a multi-service abort triggers. Normal paging stays with oncall.

bench: Any changes to rollback authority?

release-lead: No change. Oncall retains final rollback authority. Bridge can recommend and coordinate. We added a short CLI workflow to tag a rollup:

```
# nominate bridge on deploy
rdeploy tag --deploy-id DEPLOY_ID --meta bridge=nina
```

release-lead: Admins: update runbooks to mention bridge. I'll roll out a small onboarding doc and a 30-min office hours Tues 11:00 PT for questions.

nina: Ack, will update team runbook.

theo: I'll add the bridge field to our CI deploy template.

devops-bot: New policy published: https://internal.docs/releases/bridge-role. Office hours event created: Tue 11:00 PT.

release-lead: Thanks all. If anyone objects to the rollout of this policy, speak now or DM me. Otherwise we'll apply it to the next release window. :white_check_mark:
